summary: Intermittent proxy routing causes eu-west requests to traverse us-east, p95/p99 spikes and generation timeouts
description:
Issue summary: Beginning 2026-03-12 09:22 UTC we observed a recurring increase in request latencies for a subset of EU customers. Impact: p50 remained stable but p95/p99 latency increased from ~230ms to 1.2s-3.6s; some streaming sessions dropped with 504 gateway timeouts and 5xx from serving-runtime. Affected customer reported failed inference calls for user-facing endpoint.
Environment: production, eu-west region, managed routing-proxy layer, API gateway fronting.
Steps to reproduce:
1. Send batch of streaming generate requests to /v1/generate using eu-west endpoint from an EU client
2. Observe high p95 and occasional 504s during affected windows
3. Reproduces intermittently; not reproducible from inside cloud provider's eu-west internal network
Observed logs and metrics:
- Edge proxy logs show an increase in upstream connection times and TCP RTT spikes to us-east IPs
- Traces show requests entering eu-west API gateway but being proxied to a us-east serving pod (unexpected)
- No recent model rollout for the affected models; serving-runtime CPU/GPU usage normal on eu-west pools
- Cloud VPC flow logs show BGP flap between provider PoPs causing traffic engineering to shift paths
First reported by customer at 2026-03-12 09:30 UTC. SLA first-response due 2026-03-12 10:00 UTC.
Additional notes: Customer is enterprise tier with global routing policy; they rely on regional pinning but observed overrides.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 10:10 UTC - Support: Verified increased p95 with live metrics (console per-route). 2026-03-12 10:35 UTC - Eng (Jamal): Correlated proxy logs with cloud provider BGP events; identified that an intermediate edge proxy incorrectly applied overflow routing policy and sent traffic to us-east for capacity reasons. 2026-03-12 11:05 UTC - SRE: Confirmed no resource saturation on eu-west serving nodes; flags point to routing layer rewriting region header. Hypothesis: recent proxy config change (auto-failover policy v2) causes undesired cross-region fallback under transient packet loss. Evidence: proxy config commit https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/commit/abcdef; cloud provider incident REF-2206 noted similar BGP flaps. 2026-03-12 12:00 UTC - Reproduced by forcing packet loss on test path in staging; proxy rerouted to alternate region.
comments: Aisha Patel (2026-03-12 09:35 UTC): Customer BrightHire reporting high p95 and 504s for eu-west. Escalating to SRE. Marking P1.

Jamal Nguyen (2026-03-12 10:40 UTC): Found proxy behavior correlates with provider BGP events. Adding network and infra teams. Temporary mitigation: disable auto-failover on routing-proxy for enterprise customers while we investigate.
Sophie Carter (SRE) (2026-03-12 11:50 UTC): Applied config rollback on routing-proxy in eu-west. Observed p95 improve from 1.8s -> 320ms within 8 minutes. Monitoring.
Diego Morales (Customer Success) (2026-03-12 12:20 UTC): Notified BrightHire of mitigation; asked for validation on their end. Customer confirms reduced errors for now.
resolution: Mitigation: Rolled back routing-proxy auto-failover v2 in eu-west at 2026-03-12 11:30 UTC which restored regional routing and reduced latency. Root cause: proxy config combined with transient provider BGP path changes triggered cross-region fallback behavior. Follow-ups: 1) Create infra PR to add stricter region pinning for enterprise customers and add health checks before cross-region failover (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/985). 2) Request support ticket with cloud provider to get stable peering and BGP flap RCA. 3) Add automated alert to detect proxy-originated cross-region uplinks. Ticket status: monitoring post-mitigation; will move to Resolved after 48h stable.
notes_for_followup: Add e2e test that simulates packet loss without failing over to other regions, update rollout checklist to require canary behavior verification for routing policy changes, schedule postmortem with network and infra teams.
